jobs.description:
Salary Range: $77,265.00

(Min.) - $100,444.00

(Mid.) - $123,625.00

(Max.)

Established in 1997, L.A. Care Health Plan is an independent public agency created by the state of California to provide health coverage to low-income Los Angeles County residents. We are the nation’s largest publicly operated health plan. Serving more than 2 million members, we make sure our members get the right care at the right place at the right time.

Mission: L.A. Care’s mission is to provide access to quality health care for Los Angeles County's vulnerable and low-income communities and residents and to support the safety net required to achieve that purpose.

Job Summary

The Behavioral Health Treatment Program Specialist II is responsible for conducting clinical reviews of comprehensive diagnostic evaluations, Behavioral Health Treatment (BHT) plans, and related medical records. The Clinical reviewer determines medical necessity, evaluates requested service intensity against clinical severity and documented progress, and ensures appropriate documentation. The reviewer will confirm compliance with the established clinical policy and state/federal regulatory standards governing Medi-Cal Behavioral Health Treatment (BHT) services. These services apply to individuals with Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) and related conditions where individuals require Applied Behavioral Analysis (ABA) or other related BHT services. Behavioral Health Treatment Program Specialist applies clinical benchmarks and medical necessity criteria consistently and conduct peer-to-peer clinical discussions with providers as needed to coordinate care.

Duties

Conduct clinical review of comprehensive diagnostic evaluations and BHT treatment plans to determine medical necessity, clinical appropriateness, and accuracy of documentation.

Review and approve BHT/ABA treatment plans, ensuring requested services are clinically justified, properly documented, and consistent with diagnostic findings and treatment goals.

Apply BCBA-level clinical judgment to evaluate ABA service requests, treatment hours, goals, and progress notes for medical necessity and clinical soundness.

Ensure clinical determinations comply with applicable state and federal regulatory standards governing BHT/ABA referral, authorization, and documentation requirements.

Identify documentation gaps or clinical concerns in submitted records and communicate findings to providers and internal UM/claims staff.

Perform other duties as assigned.

Duties Continued

Education Required

Master's Degree in Psychology or Applied Behavior Analysis or Related Field

Education Preferred

Bachelor's Degree

Experience

Required:

At least 2 years of experience as a BCBA with ABA services, assessments, treatment, programing, and familiarity with regulations.

Experience in face-to-face ABA case management in the field.

Skills

Required:

Understand the Early Periodic Screening Detection & Treatment (EPSDT) process and the eligibility criteria.

Proficient in reviewing progress reports and assessing appropriateness of clinical treatment and recommendations.

Excellent verbal, written communication and presentation skills.

Proficient in Microsoft Office and computer skills

Licenses/Certifications Required

Board Certified Behavioral Analyst - Active, current and unrestricted California license.

Licenses/Certifications Preferred

And/Or any of the following Licenses/ Certifications:

Licensed Pharmacy Doctorate/Psychology Doctorate - Active, current and unrestricted California

Licensed Clinical Social Worker (LCSW) - Active, current and unrestricted California License

Licensed Marriage and Family Therapy (LMFT) - Active, current and unrestricted California License

Required Training

Physical Requirements

Light

Additional Information

The expected pay range is based on many factors such as geography, experience, education, and the market. The range is subject to change.

This position is a limited duration position. The term of this position is a minimum one year and maximum of two years from the start date unless terminated earlier by either party. Limited duration positions are full-time positions and are eligible to receive full benefits.

jobs.title: Program Manager of Community Nutrition and Food as Medicine Initiatives
jobs.description:
Guided by our mission of Feeding Neighbors, Nourishing Community, 4Saints Episcopal Food Pantry serves Fort Worth’s historic East Lancaster Avenue area by addressing the critical Social Determinants of Health (SDOH) that shape our community's well-being.

Located in a designated food desert, East Lancaster residents face systemic barriers to affordable, nutritious food—directly driving elevated rates of diet-related chronic illness and food insecurity.
4Saints acts as a bridge between healthcare systems and daily life. We address key Social Determinants of Health (SDOH) by pairing a dignified, client-choice food market with targeted clinical partnerships. By translating clinical care into accessible, nutritious food, practical education, and ongoing support, we empower neighbors to take control of their health in a welcoming, community-rooted environment.

Program Manager of Community Nutrition and Food as Medicine Initiatives

Position Type:
Full-Time / Grant-Funded (Initial 2-Year Term with renewal potential)

Position Summary:

The Program Manager of Community Nutrition and Food as Medicine Initiatives serves as 4Saints’ clinical and community nutrition leader, bridging community food access with measurable healthcare outcomes.

Reporting directly to the Executive Director, this role operates at two interconnected levels:
Shaping a high-nutrition food environment for all pantry guests.
Leading the continued growth of 4Saints' Food as Medicine initiative through the F.I.T. (Food as an Integrated Treatment) program.

As a Licensed Registered Dietitian, the Manager uses a dual approach to community health: driving broad-impact nutrition education, culinary classes, and pantry-wide strategic food sourcing, while providing high-touch 1:1 Medical Nutrition Therapy for F.I.T. program participants.

Working in close partnership with the Director of Operations (who manages physical facility operations, equipment, and inventory logistics), the Manager ensures that food procurement supports therapeutic health goals. As 4Saints expands its health initiatives, this position will also provide operational direction and supervision for growing program support staff, interdisciplinary team members, and academic interns.

This is a unique opportunity for an innovative Registered Dietitian to help shape an emerging Food as Medicine program. The Program Manager will have significant autonomy in designing systems, developing community partnerships, and building a sustainable model that integrates nutrition care with measurable health outcomes.

Key Responsibilities:

Community Health & Pantry- Wide Nutrition (Broad Impact)

Class & Workshop Facilitation:
Lead and conduct interactive group classes, workshops, and cooking demonstrations—focusing on nutrition education, chronic disease self-management (e.g., diabetes, hypertension), and practical culinary skills for pantry guests.
Choice-Based Market Experience:
Utilize 4Saints’ market floor to provide point-of-choice nutrition education, designing educational shelf-tagging, visual cues, and tours that help participants translate program concepts into independent grocery shopping habits.
Resource & Content Creation:
Author, design, and curate culturally responsive recipes, shopping guides, communication releases, class materials, and educational handouts in English and Spanish.

Food Ordering, Sourcing & Inventory Curation (In Partnership with Operations)

Food Procurement Leadership:
Provide nutritional leadership for pantry food procurement by guiding the selection and ordering of foods that support both community nutrition and therapeutic dietary goals. Work collaboratively with the Director of Operations on purchasing logistics, inventory capacity, and budget management.
Supplemental Sourcing & Vendor Vetting:
Research, vet, and establish alternative food sourcing channels (local growers, commercial distributors, food rescue networks) to supplement food bank offerings—ensuring consistent inventory/supply of high nutritional value foods for all clients.
Pantry Nutrition Curation:
Select and curate food items offered on the market floor, balancing core nutritious staples for broad pantry guests with specialized, medically tailored options (low-sodium, low-glycemic, DASH-compliant) required for F.I.T. participants.
Operational Alignment:
Work in close coordination with the Director of Operations to ensure placed orders align with established food budgets, storage/cold-chain capacity, and floor restocking workflows.

F.I.T. Program Leadership & Clinic Care (Targeted Impact)

F.I.T. Program Scaling:
Lead the continued expansion of the F.I.T. (Food as an Integrated Treatment) program, building upon its successful pilot phase to establish a sustainable Food as Medicine model that improves community health outcomes.
1:1 Clinical Coaching:
Conduct scheduled 1:1 consultations and follow-up Medical Nutrition Therapy (MNT) coaching sessions with F.I.T. participants—translating biometric data into tailored, goal-oriented health plans.
Closed-Loop Referral Pathways:
Design and refine workflows that translate incoming healthcare referrals and biometric data (e.g., blood pressure, A1C, cholesterol) into personalized market guidelines and client care plans.
Clinical Outcomes Tracking & Reporting:
Serve as primary liaison for data exchange with healthcare partners, tracking participant health metrics to evaluate and report clinical outcomes.

Organizational Leadership & Program Growth

Interdisciplinary Coordination:
Lead and coordinate multidisciplinary care strategies, integrating behavior-change models, health coaching methodologies, and client accountability practices as programming expands.
Team Supervision & Development:
Provide oversight, training, and direct supervision for designated program support personnel, health education staff, dietetic interns, academic rotations and volunteers.
Partnership Expansion:
Seek out and build strategic alliances with healthcare systems, community organizations, and specialized food suppliers to expand general pantry and Food as Medicine (F.I.T) program reach.
Organizational Alignment:
Collaborate effectively with Executive Leadership to align Food as Medicine initiatives with overarching organizational goals and evolving operational structures.
Culture & Equity:
Embed 4Saints’ commitment to dignity, respect, equity, and trauma-informed care across all participant touchpoints and operational workflows.

Qualifications & Requirements:

Required:

Credentials:
Active Registered Dietitian (RD/RDN) credential and current State of Texas Dietitian License (or immediate eligibility for Texas licensure).
Education:
Bachelor's degree in Nutrition, Dietetics, Public Health, or a closely related field. Master's degree preferred.
Clinical Knowledge:
Practical experience delivering Medical Nutrition Therapy (MNT) for diabetes, metabolic conditions, and other therapeutic diets in a community-based setting.
Systems & Leadership Mindset:
Ability to build patient workflows, manage partner data exchanges, and lead interdisciplinary health teams or support staff.

Highly Preferred:

Language:
Bilingual fluency in Spanish and English (verbal and written) strongly preferred.
Experience:
2+ years in community nutrition, public health, ambulatory care, or clinical settings—with experience in client-choice pantry settings, hands-on cooking/shopping education, or vendor procurement.
Behavioral Health Expertise:
Experience applying behavior-change theories and health coaching methodologies preferred. Active credentials such as Certified Health & Wellness Coach (CHWC) or Certified Health Education Specialist (CHES) are considered a strong asset.
Supervisory Aptitude:
Demonstrated capacity to mentor, supervise, or lead direct reports, health coaches, students, or multidisciplinary team members.

Success in this role:

During the first year, the Program Manager will be expected to:
Expand participation in the F.I.T. Food as Medicine program.
Deliver engaging nutrition education and culinary programming for pantry guests.
Strengthen nutrition standards and strategic food procurement across the pantry.
Build and maintain referral partnerships with healthcare providers.
Track participant health outcomes and support grant reporting.
Help establish 4Saints as a regional leader in community-based Food as Medicine initiatives.

Compensation & Benefits:

Base Salary:
$55k–70k, commensurate with experience and qualifications
Performance Incentive Plan:
Opportunity to earn up to an additional 10% annual performance bonus, structured as:
5% linked to individual goal attainment (as defined by executive leadership).
5% contingent on the achievement of key organizational strategic objectives.

Annual Review:
Eligible for annual merit reviews (3–5% performance-based growth).
Technology Allowance:
$25 per month technology stipend.
Paid Time Off (PTO) & Leave:

3 weeks (15 days) of Paid Time Off (PTO).
10 days of paid sick/personal leave.
10 paid holidays (9 fixed holidays + 1 floating holiday).

Discretionary Holiday Leave:
One week off between Christmas and New Year's Day, subject to executive discretion and the operational requirements of 4Saints Episcopal Food Pantry.
Hybrid:
Work environment

jobs.title: Program Manager, Mental Health Outpatient
Program Coordinator
jobs.description:
Who We Are

At ERC Pathlight, we’re on a mission to change lives—and we’re looking for people who feel called to do the same.

As one of the nation’s leading treatment providers for eating disorders and mood, anxiety, and trauma-related conditions, we bring innovative, evidence-based, and deeply compassionate care to patients across the country. With multiple locations nationwide and extensive virtual programming, we meet patients exactly where they are and help them move toward lasting recovery.

Founded in 2008 by renowned psychiatrists and psychologists, ERC Pathlight now supports more than 6,000 patients each year. And as the need for world-class mental health care continues to rise, our commitment is stronger than ever: to expand access, elevate the standard of care, and empower every patient to rebuild their life with dignity and hope.

Why Join Us

When you join ERC Pathlight, you become part of a team that shows up every day to make a real difference. You’ll work alongside passionate clinicians, dedicated support staff, and mission-driven leaders who believe in collaboration, growth, and doing the right thing—always.

Here, your work matters. Your ideas matter. You
matter.

If you’re energized by purpose, motivated by impact, and ready to help transform the future of mental health treatment, you belong here.

Come build hope. Come save lives. Come grow with us.

What You’ll Be Doing

Schedule:Fulltime NOC PC 6:30pm-7am Tue/Fri/Sun

The Program Coordinator (PC I, PC II, PC III) is responsible for providing direct care and supervision to patients within inpatient, residential, and partial hospitalization levels of care at ERC Pathlight. Program Coordinators maintain a safe, structured, and therapeutic milieu while supporting the implementation of individualized treatment plans.

PCs provide patient supervision, maintain structure and boundaries, support therapeutic programming, assist with mealtime support, and complete required documentation. Level placement (I, II, III) is determined based on education, experience, and demonstrated competency.

Essential Duties And Responsibilities

Milieu Management
Maintain daily program structure by following the established schedule
Complete observation rounds and safety checks as ordered by physician
Support patients with de-escalation and implementation of coping skills per treatment plan
Conduct room and luggage searches
Supervise fresh air breaks and mindful movement exposures
Provide ongoing bathroom monitoring
Obtain and document patient vital signs, weights, and urine specific gravity (as applicable by location/program)
Group Facilitation
Participate in facilitation of therapeutic groups
Complete required EHR documentation related to group facilitation
Support group-based social activities and meal outings
Meal Support 
Participate in all meals and snacks with patients 
Provide meal support using coaching and skills aligned with the treatment team 
Complete timely and accurate meal-related documentation 
Support dietitians in preparation for Nutrition and Cooking Groups 
Ensure adherence to individualized meal plans and allergy-safety protocols 
Support restaurant outings as needed 
Administrative & Operational Support 
Complete required documentation in compliance with organizational and regulatory standards, including patient observations, meals, and shift-related events 
Provide patient transportation for medical appointments (as applicable by location/program) 
Support additional transportation needs including outings, grocery procurement, or other facility needs 
Assist with food procurement as needed (may occur weekly) 
Distribute mail and packages daily 

Position Expectations (All Levels) 

All Program Coordinators must:
Be willing and able to work at all ERC Pathlight local sites as assigned
Be compliant with certification and regulatory requirements for each practice location
Maintain a flexible schedule to meet organizational staffing needs
Be available to work weekends and holidays as required
Be available to work on-call shifts based on business needs and in accordance with applicable federal, state, and local labor laws

Must Haves

Program Coordinator I (PC I)

High School Diploma or GED (Required)
Entry-level role: no prior direct patient care experience required unless required by state regulation (Required)
Valid driver’s license with safe driving record: required only at locations operating company vehicles or requiring driving on behalf of the company (Required)
Washington teammates must hold a state credential (may be pending at time of hire) (Required)
ServSafe certification may be required depending on state and local licensing regulations (Required)
Mental Health/Psych Tech or CNA certification (Preferred)

Program Coordinator II (PC II)

High School Diploma or GED (Required)
Minimum of one (1) year of direct patient care experience (Required)
Valid driver’s license with safe driving record: required only at locations operating company vehicles or requiring driving on behalf of the company (Required)
Washington teammates must hold a state credential (may be pending at time of hire) (Required)
ServSafe certification may be required depending on state and local licensing regulations (Required) 
Mental Health/Psych Tech or CAN certification (Preferred) 

Program Coordinator III (PC III)

Bachelor’s degree in behavioral health or related field (Required)
Minimum of six (6) months of experience in a behavioral health or related field (Required)
Valid driver’s license with safe driving record: required only at locations operating company vehicles or requiring driving on behalf of the company (Required)
Washington teammates must hold a state credential (may be pending at time of hire) (Required) 
ServSafe certification may be required depending on state and local licensing regulations (Required) 
Mental Health/Psych Tech or CAN certification (Preferred)

#ERC

The compensation range for this position is based upon candidate experience and market expectations.

Illinois Pay Range

$18.25 - $29 USD

What We Offer

At ERC Pathlight, caring for people is our mission and that begins with caring for our own team. Your well-being matters, and our benefit program is designed to support every part of your life.

We offer competitive compensation; comprehensive medical, dental, and vision coverage; generous Paid Time Off; Parental Leave benefits; Retirement benefits; and tuition reimbursement to help you continue growing in your career.

We also recognize that mental health is part of every person’s experience. That’s why we strive to create a workplace where you feel supported, seen, and encouraged—personally, professionally, and at home.

When you thrive, you can do your best work. And your best work changes lives.
